title: The Affine-Group Model of the Galois Action
content: The splitting field of X⁵−2 is ℚ(⁵√2, ζ₅), and its Galois group permutes the five roots α·ζ₅ᵏ. Labelling each root by its exponent k ∈ 𝔽₅ = Fin 5, the action becomes the affine group AGL(1,𝔽₅) = {x ↦ a·x + b : a ∈ 𝔽₅ˣ, b ∈ 𝔽₅}. Multiplying roots by ζ₅ is the translation x ↦ x+1; the Frobenius automorphism ζ₅ ↦ ζ₅² is multiplication by 2. This docstring fixes the dictionary between field theory and the permutation calculus that follows.

title: σ — The Translation 5-Cycle
content: σ is the permutation x ↦ x+1 on Fin 5, i.e. the 5-cycle (0 1 2 3 4). It is given explicitly as an `Equiv.Perm` by its forward table ![1,2,3,4,0] and inverse table ![4,0,1,2,3], with the two round-trip laws discharged by `decide`. In the affine picture σ is the translation b=1, corresponding to multiplying every root by the primitive 5th root of unity ζ₅.
mathContext: $\sigma: x \mapsto x+1 \pmod 5$, the cycle $(0\,1\,2\,3\,4)$; as a root map $\alpha\zeta_5^k \mapsto \alpha\zeta_5^{k+1}$.

title: τ — The Multiply-by-2 4-Cycle
content: τ is the permutation x ↦ 2·x on Fin 5 = 𝔽₅, the 4-cycle (1 2 4 3) fixing 0. Its forward table is ![0,2,4,1,3]. Since 2 is a primitive root modulo 5, its powers 2,4,3,1 run through all of 𝔽₅ˣ, so τ has order 4. In the affine picture τ is the multiplier a=2, corresponding to the Frobenius automorphism ζ₅ ↦ ζ₅².
mathContext: $\tau: x \mapsto 2x \pmod 5$; $2^1=2,\,2^2=4,\,2^3=3,\,2^4=1$, so $2$ is a primitive root and $\tau$ fixes $0$ while 4-cycling $\{1,2,3,4\}$.

title: Base Relations by `decide`
content: The elementary facts σ⁵ = 1, σ ≠ 1, τ² ≠ 1, τ⁴ = 1 are each proved by unfolding the explicit permutation and calling `decide`. Because Perm (Fin 5) has decidable equality and the tables are concrete, these reduce to finite kernel computations — no group-theoretic reasoning is needed for the raw relations. The τ facts are phrased with exponents 2^1 and 2^(1+1) to feed directly into `orderOf_eq_prime_pow` below.

title: The Defining Normalizing Relation τστ⁻¹ = σ²
content: This is the single relation that pins down F₂₀. Conjugating the 5-cycle σ by the 4-cycle τ squares it, expressing that ⟨τ⟩ ≅ C₄ acts on the normal subgroup ⟨σ⟩ ≅ C₅ by the automorphism x ↦ 2x. Because 2 has order 4 in 𝔽₅ˣ, this action is faithful, so the semidirect product C₅ ⋊ C₄ is the full Frobenius group F₂₀ rather than a smaller quotient. Everything downstream (orders, count, transitivity) flows from this identity.
mathContext: $\tau\sigma\tau^{-1} = \sigma^2$; equivalently the conjugation action sends the generator $1 \in C_5$ to $2\in C_5$, an order-4 automorphism of $C_5$.

title: Orders of the Generators via Prime / Prime-Power Criteria
content: orderOf σ = 5 follows from `orderOf_eq_prime`: a nonidentity element whose fifth power is the identity has order the prime 5. orderOf τ = 4 uses `orderOf_eq_prime_pow` with p=2, n=1: an element with τ^(2²)=1 but τ^2≠1 has order exactly 2²=4. The `Fact (Nat.Prime …)` instances supply the primality side conditions these lemmas require.

title: Base Commutation τσᵐ = σ²ᵐτ
content: `tau_sigma_pow` moves a single τ past an arbitrary power σᵐ, doubling the exponent: τ·σᵐ = σ^(2m)·τ. The base case τσ = σ²τ is obtained from the defining relation by right-multiplying by τ (the `group` tactic normalizes the conjugation). Induction on m then slides τ across one σ at a time, each step converting τσ into σ²τ and accumulating the doubling. This is the m-direction of the semidirect multiplication rule.

title: The Full Semidirect-Product Commutation Law
content: `tau_pow_sigma_pow` generalizes to arbitrary powers of both generators: τⁿ·σᵐ = σ^(2ⁿm)·τⁿ. Induction on n peels off one τ (invoking the base commutation, which contributes a factor of 2 to the exponent) and reassembles the τⁿ⁺¹. This identity IS the multiplication table of C₅ ⋊ C₄: it lets any word in σ and τ be normalized to the canonical form σⁱτʲ, which is exactly what makes the 20-element count achievable.
mathContext: $\tau^n \sigma^m = \sigma^{2^n m}\tau^n$; the exponent multiplier $2^n$ traces the $C_4$-action $x \mapsto 2x$ iterated $n$ times.

title: F20 as the Explicit Set {σⁱτʲ}
content: Rather than take ⟨σ,τ⟩ abstractly, F20 is defined directly as the carrier {g | ∃ i j, g = σⁱτʲ}, and the subgroup axioms are proved by hand. Closure under multiplication uses the full commutation law to rewrite σⁱτʲ·σᵏτˡ back into canonical form σ^(i+2ʲk)τ^(j+l). Closure under inverses uses σ⁻¹ = σ⁴ and τ⁻¹ = τ³ (from the order relations) to express (σⁱτʲ)⁻¹ as another σ-power times τ-power. Making the carrier explicit is what enables the surjection-based upper bound.

title: F20 Equals the Generated Subgroup ⟨σ,τ⟩
content: `closure_eq` proves Subgroup.closure {σ,τ} = F20 by antisymmetry. The ⊆ direction is immediate since σ = σ¹τ⁰ and τ = σ⁰τ¹ both lie in the explicit carrier. The ⊇ direction shows every σⁱτʲ is reachable from the generators using `pow_mem` and `mul_mem`. This bridges the hand-built set F20 to the standard notion of the subgroup generated by {σ,τ}, so results about F20 transfer to ⟨σ,τ⟩.
mathContext: $\langle\sigma,\tau\rangle = F_{20}$; both inclusions via generators lying in $F_{20}$ and $F_{20}$ being closed.

title: |F20| = 20 by Matching Upper and Lower Bounds
content: The main count squeezes |F20| between 20 and 20. The upper bound |F20| ≤ 20 comes from a surjection Fin 5 × Fin 4 ↠ F20 sending (i,j) to σⁱτʲ — well-defined because σ⁵=τ⁴=1 let exponents be reduced mod 5 and mod 4 (`pow_mod_orderOf`). The lower bound 20 ∣ |F20| comes from Lagrange: the coprime element orders 5 and 4 both divide |F20|, so their product 20 does too (`Nat.Coprime.mul_dvd_of_dvd_of_dvd`). Antisymmetry of ≤ gives exactly 20. Note that divisibility alone (20 ∣ |F20| ∣ 120) cannot pin the value — the semidirect structure is essential for the upper bound.
mathContext: $20 \mid |F_{20}| \le 20 \Rightarrow |F_{20}| = 20$; upper via surjection $\mathrm{Fin}\,5 \times \mathrm{Fin}\,4 \twoheadrightarrow F_{20}$, lower via $\mathrm{lcm}(5,4)=20$.

title: Transitivity of the Action on the Five Roots
content: `acts_transitively` shows the orbit of the label 0 is all of Fin 5: the translation power σˣ maps 0 to x, and σˣ ∈ F20. So the subgroup generated by translations alone already acts transitively on the roots. This matches the irreducibility of X⁵−2 over ℚ — the Galois group of an irreducible polynomial acts transitively on its roots — and sets up the orbit–stabilizer decomposition 20 = |orbit|·|stab| = 5·4.
mathContext: $\forall x,\ \sigma^x \cdot 0 = x$, so the orbit of $0$ is all of $\mathbb{F}_5$; transitivity $\Leftrightarrow$ irreducibility of $X^5-2$.
